Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Insurance Group Q2 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Horizon Insurance Group's Q2 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Claims Officer; and Amanda Ruiz, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Horizon Insurance Group's performance for Q2. We delivered strong results, driven by favorable reserve development trends, robust reinsurance recoveries received and expected, improving customer acquisition cost trends, the positive impact of pricing changes on premium volume, favorable expense ratio trends and drivers, strong new business production volume, meaningful share repurchase activity, and the effectiveness of our reinsurance program. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Michael Rivera, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $485 million, or $2.15 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included favorable reserve development, reinsurance recoveries, customer acquisition efficiencies, pricing-driven premium growth, expense improvements, new business momentum, share repurchases, and reinsurance effectiveness. Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $285 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with 250% RBC. Our expense ratio also improved to 28.5%.

Let me kick off the financial review by diving into our reserve development trends, which continue to be a cornerstone of our earnings quality and a testament to our disciplined reserving philosophy. For those new to our calls, reserve development reflects the difference between our initial loss reserves established at the end of each accident year and the actual payments and adjustments we make as claims mature. Favorable development occurs when actual losses come in below our original estimates, allowing us to release reserves into earnings, while unfavorable development requires reserve strengthening.

In Q2, we reported net favorable reserve development of $185 million, bringing our year-to-date total to $420 million. This compares favorably to $142 million in Q2 2023 and $380 million YTD last year, representing a 30% acceleration in releases. On a calendar-year basis, this equates to a 2.8-point boost to our combined ratio for the quarter, landing us at an accident-year ex-cat combined ratio of 92.4%, right in line with our target of sub-93%. This favorable trend held across 85% of our portfolio, driven by better-than-expected loss emergence in personal lines and legacy commercial casualty years.

Breaking it down by accident year, our development was broadly positive for all years prior to 2022. For accident year 2021, our largest cohort at $2.8 billion in initial net reserves, we saw $92 million of favorable development, primarily from lower-than-anticipated severity in workers' compensation and general liability. This vintage continues to outperform our Bornhuetter-Ferguson models by 4.2 points on ultimate loss ratio, thanks to proactive claims management and a moderation in social inflation following the peaks from Talc and Roundup litigation. For accident year 2022, we released $68 million favorably, offset slightly by $15 million unfavorable in property from Hurricane Ian tail claims. For 2023, development was modestly favorable at $42 million, reflecting stable auto frequency trends but with careful monitoring of repair inflation.

By line of business, personal auto, which comprises 35% of our net premiums earned, delivered the strongest performance with $110 million favorable, or 3.5 points to the loss ratio. We've seen severity stabilize at 8% year-over-year growth, below our 10% actuary pricing assumption, due to parts deflation from increased Chinese imports and our partnership with CCC Intelligent Solutions for AI-driven repair estimating. Homeowners followed with $65 million favorable, buoyed by lower weather-related water damage claims amid a mild Q2 severe convective storm season.

Commercial lines showed mixed results: $75 million favorable overall, led by workers' comp at $45 million, where return-to-work programs and telemedicine integrations reduced indemnity costs by 12%. However, we strengthened reserves by $22 million in excess & umbrella casualty, reflecting emerging social inflation in litigation-heavy states like California and New York, such as third-party rideshare claims similar to Uber's reserve pressures. Our commercial auto book saw neutral development, as higher medical inflation in no-fault states like Florida offset frequency declines from telematics adoption.

Regionally, our U.S. operations, 72% of the portfolio, drove 78% of the favorable releases, with the Southeast and Midwest shining brightest. In California, we took a prudent $18 million unfavorable hit from the 2023 Zogg Fire tail and ongoing rebuild delays, but our exposure there is now just 4% of total property risks following our 15% quota share reinsurance renewal with Swiss Re. Europe contributed $35 million favorable, particularly in UK motor where Ogden rate tweaks and IFRS 17 implementation have sharpened our IBNR triangles. Asia-Pacific was flat, with $12 million unfavorable in Australian flood reopeners, but our Japan P&C book benefited from $20 million releases as COVID-related business interruption claims fully closed out.

What's behind these trends? First, our technical edge: we've invested $45 million over the past 18 months in our ResQ AI platform, a proprietary machine learning tool built on top of Emblem Claims Analytics and integrated with Duck Creek, improving case reserve adequacy by 15% and reducing tail risk in long-tail lines like D&O, where we've seen favorable development in 90% of accident years since 2019. Second, macroeconomic tailwinds: medical cost trends cooled to 4.5% from 6.2% YoY per our Milliman benchmarking, and construction labor inflation eased post-Fed hikes. Third, catastrophe normalization: no major events this quarter versus Ian and Ida last year, allowing prior cat reserves to normalize.

Strategically, we're hardening our reserving assumptions: ultimate loss picks now embed 1.5 points more for social inflation across casualty, informed by peer reviews like Travelers' $500 million Q1 strengthening. Pricing discipline remains key, with our 9.2% commercial renewal rate increase outpacing 7.1% loss cost trends per Verisk analytics. Reinsurance optimization helped too: our $1.2 billion catastrophe aggregate tower with RenaissanceRe capped property unfavorable development at 0.5 points. Looking forward, we expect $350-450 million favorable development for FY24, assuming no black swan catastrophes, but we're stress-testing for 20% social inflation spikes as seen in Chubb's disclosures.

This reserve development underscores the strength of our $18.7 billion balance sheet and 250% reserve leverage ratio, well above peers like Progressive at 220%. This positions us to deploy $600 million in buybacks this year while growing book value per share 12%.

Before moving on, I'd like to dive deeper into another key component of our loss reserve development and earnings profile: reinsurance recoveries received and expected. Reinsurance is a cornerstone of our risk management strategy at Horizon, allowing us to optimize capital deployment across our Property & Casualty and Specialty Lines portfolios while maintaining a robust 250% combined ratio target for the year.

In Q2 2024, we recognized $285 million in reinsurance recoveries received, up 18% year-over-year from $241 million in Q2 2023. This brings our year-to-date total to $512 million, a 22% increase from $420 million in the first half of 2023. These recoveries directly contributed 12 points of favorable development to our underlying loss ratio, helping us deliver a calendar-year combined ratio of 92.4%, our strongest Q2 performance since 2019.

Paid recoveries totaled $265 million in the quarter, primarily from our excess-of-loss catastrophe programs. This includes $112 million related to Hurricane Idalia's remnants in the Southeast U.S. last September, where we finalized settlements with our lead reinsurer, Swiss Re, at a 98% recovery rate on ceded losses. We also collected $68 million from the 2023 California wildfires under our layered quota-share treaty with Munich Re, reflecting quicker-than-expected subrogation and IBNR settlements.

On the expected recoveries side, we now project $410 million outstanding as of June 30, 2024, down from $465 million at year-end 2023. This represents a $55 million reduction quarter-over-quarter, driven by $30 million in favorable prior-year development and accelerated billing cycles. Of this balance, 65% or $267 million is deemed highly probable under ASC 944, with collection timelines averaging 9-12 months. The remainder is tied to ongoing arbitrations, notably $45 million from the 2022 European Windstorm Fiona under our aggregate cover with Berkshire Hathaway Re.

Our recovery rate on gross ceded losses improved to 96% in Q2, up from 94% last year, thanks to proactive portfolio actions. Catastrophe-driven recoveries accounted for 72% of the total, with the balance from attritional lines like Workers' Comp and D&O.

Regionally, North America, representing 55% of our ceded premium at $2.8 billion annually, saw U.S. recoveries surge 25% YoY to $157 million, fueled by secondary perils like severe convective storms in the Midwest, such as the April tornado outbreaks in Oklahoma and Texas. We've seen reinsurers like RenaissanceRe honor 100% of our parametric triggers on these events, validating our $500 million sidecar issuance earlier this year.

In Europe and Bermuda, 28% of recoveries at $80 million stemmed from flood events in Germany and the Benelux region, where our proportional treaties with Hannover Re yielded a 97% recovery amid softening reinstatement premium terms post-2023. Asia-Pacific contributed 12% or $34 million, primarily typhoon-related from Japan, with expected flows from our 40% quota-share on our $1.2 billion Japanese earthquake book ceded to PartnerRe. Emerging markets like LatAm added $14 million, but we're tempering expectations there due to currency volatility in Brazil, where recoveries from last year's floods are at 85% realization versus 95% globally.

Technical initiatives have been pivotal: we've rolled out an AI-enhanced claims adjudication platform in partnership with Guidewire, reducing billing disputes by 30% and shortening collection cycles from 18 to 12 months. This integrates real-time cat modeling from RMS v17.1, improving our loss reserve estimates by 8% accuracy on U.S. hurricane layers. Additionally, our multi-year reinsurance renewals at January 1, locking in $4.2 billion of limit at a 5% net cost versus 7% in 2023, include performance-based collateral clauses that have unlocked $25 million in early cash this quarter.

Strategically, we're leaning into risk-adequate pricing and retentions. Post-Hurricane Helene's landfall last week, we're modeling $150-200 million in gross losses, 80% reinsured above our $50 million retention, expecting $120-160 million in future recoveries booked pro-rata. We've diversified our panel, reducing single-reinsurer exposure from 22% to 15% with new capacity from SCOR and Lloyd's syndicates. This hardening market, with cat reinsurance rates up 10-15% at the June 1 renewals, positions us to earn higher ceding commissions, targeting 25% on our $6.5 billion gross written premium.

Looking forward, we expect full-year 2024 recoveries received of $1.1-1.2 billion, implying 5-10% YoY growth, with Q3 weighted toward $350 million from prior-year cats. Expected balances should decline to $300 million by year-end as arbitrations resolve. This supports our raised EPS guidance to $4.85-$5.15 and ROE of 14-15%.

Next, as we look at operational metrics, customer acquisition cost trends, or CAC, are a critical lever for our long-term profitability in this competitive landscape. CAC is calculated as our total sales and marketing expenses, including digital advertising, agent commissions, partnership fees, and lead generation costs, divided by the number of new policies written. We're reporting this on a per-policy basis to normalize for our multi-line portfolio across personal lines like auto, home, and renters, as well as our growing commercial segments.

In Q2, our blended CAC came in at $218 per new policy, marking a 14% year-over-year decline from $253 in Q2 2023, and a sequential improvement of 6% from Q1. This is our lowest quarterly CAC in over three years, driven by channel optimization, technological efficiencies, and favorable market dynamics. On a trailing 12-month basis, CAC has declined 11% to $225, ahead of our full-year guidance of a 9-10% reduction.

By product line, auto CAC fell to $185, down 16% YoY, benefiting from our aggressive digital shift, now 62% of new auto policies acquired via direct-to-consumer channels like our mobile app and website, up from 48% last year. Homeowners CAC improved 8% sequentially to $312, as we layered in more cross-sell opportunities from existing auto customers. Commercial lines saw CAC rise modestly to $456 due to higher broker commissions amid softening rates in small business P&C, but we're mitigating this through our Horizon Business Hub platform.

Regionally, U.S. CAC at $210 dropped 15% YoY, fueled by telematics adoption rates hitting 28% for new auto policies, enhanced with our proprietary AI-driven risk scoring. In Canada, $235 flat YoY, offset by partnerships like embedded insurance with RBC for home policies. Europe showed CAC at €198 ($215 equivalent), down 12% YoY via GDPR-compliant personalization on our Euronet platform, with strong UK performance post-Brexit. Asia-Pacific had elevated CAC at A$320 ($210 USD) from agent network investments in India and Indonesia, but digital channels deliver 25% lower costs.

Driving these trends: our Horizon AI Engine for hyper-targeted ad buys on Google, Meta, and programmatic platforms reduced cost-per-lead by 22% to $18.50, with conversion rates up 9% to 14.2%. Our SmartQuote tool using alternative data cut quote abandonment by 31%. Embedded insurance now 15% of acquisitions, like Uber rideshare and Shopify SMB cyber, at $142 CAC, 40% below standalone. Agent portal with Salesforce CRM boosted submissions per agent by 18%, trimming variable commissions from 32% to 27% of CAC.

Market tailwinds: softening auto loss trends allowed competitive pricing without discounting. Our LTV:CAC ratio at 4.8x, up from 4.2x, ahead of peers. For Q3, expect $215-$220 CAC, full-year down 12-13%, with 2024 further 8-10% decline, prioritizing LTV via retention at 87% through churn modeling and Apex Rewards-like programs, plus UBI pilots.

Turning to the impact of our disciplined pricing actions on net written premium volume: premiums grew 9.2% year-over-year to $14.7 billion, our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit constant-dollar growth excluding FX. Of that, 10.5% from earned rate increases offset by 1.3% policy count decline. Average rate change +10.5%, up from +9.8% in Q1, driven by renewals in personal auto and homeowners with inflation passthroughs averaging 12-15%.

Personal Lines (55% of premiums) expanded 11.8% to $8.1 billion: auto +13.2% via HorizonDrive telematics at 28% penetration, segmenting safe drivers at 5-7% discounts, high-risk at 20-25%; retention 87.2%, new business moderated 4%. Homeowners +11.5%, with RMS modeling justifying 18% in Florida/Texas.

Commercial Lines (35%) +7.9% to $5.2 billion, pricing +9.1%: workers' comp/GL +12%, E&S +14%. Volume dipped 1.1%, offset by broker partnerships adding 2,500 risks.

U.S. (72%) +11.8% rates, 12.4% growth despite California non-renewals. Europe +3.5% flatter from motor softening. Asia-Pacific +14.2%.

AI pricing elasticity models optimize mix, shifting to high-margin E&S. Q3 pricing +10%, volume stabilizing; FY25 8-10% growth.

On expense ratio trends: 28.5%, 170 bps YoY improvement from 30.2%, sixth straight quarter better. Core ex-one-time 150 bps better; T12M 28.7%, FY guide 28.0-28.5%.

Commissions/policy acquisition 12.8%, down 50 bps YoY: U.S. personal steady at 14.2% but 80 bps clawed via incentives; agents to 11.5%. Direct digital +25% YoY shifts mix. Europe UK motor 14.1%; Asia 10.2%.

Operating costs 15.7%, down 220 bps: $450M InsureNext roadmap, 70% deployed, $120M YTD savings. 85% STP auto claims <$5k, 25% faster cycles, 12% U.S. headcount cut. RPA policy servicing -40% touchpoints. Cloud IT per policy -18%. U.S. 16.1%, Europe 15.4%, Asia 14.8%.

Ahead: $50-60M H2 savings, 75% STP; combined 95.2%.

New business production: APE $2.8B +18% YoY, 1.25M policies +22%. PVNBP $4.2B +16%, margins 28.5%.

P&C 55% $1.54B +21%: auto $850M +25% telematics; home $420M +19% parametric. Commercial $270M +12%.

Life & Health 35% $980M +14%, 750k policies: life $620M +17% IUL/direct; group $360M +9%.

Annuities $220M +25%, 45k contracts.

Regions: NA 68% $1.9B +20%; Europe 18% +12%; APAC 22% +35% India; LatAm 6% +8%.

Digital 65%, persistency 92%. Q4 APE $2.9-3.1B, FY 16-17%.

Share repurchase: $750M Q3, YTD $2.8B, 4.2% shares at $48.75 avg, vs TBVPS $46.20. 60% open market, 40% ASR Goldman. Remaining $2.2B + post-Q $250M. RBC 620%, liquidity $1.7B.

U.S. P&C 70%; Europe life $450M capital. Opportunistic below 11-13x P/E (now 10.4x). Q4 $1-1.5B.

Finally, reinsurance program effectiveness: ceded premium 24.7% or $2.8B 9M; recoveries $850M YTD, 71% cat retention vs industry 65%. Net loss 58.2%.

Layers: prop 25% QS Swiss Re; cat tower $500M xs$500M Munich/RenRe 4.2% RoL; $750M xs$1B 18 reinsurers + $300M cat bond; ILWs $400M xs$10B.

PML 8.2% 1-200yr. NA $420M recov Helene/Milton; Europe flood $120M; APAC quake 3% net.

AI response -15 days notice; 15% multi-year; no reinsurer >12%, 95% collateral.

Freed $1.1B surplus, RBC 250%, Solvency II 195%. Optimize attachments +10%; $150M EMEA cyber sidecar.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal auto and homeowners lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-driven underwriting models like ResQ and data-driven pricing strategies informed by Verisk and RMS analytics.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives, with our floating-rate portfolio yielding over 5% and duration at 5.2 years, supporting strong investment income.

David Patel: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including the AI-enhanced adjudication platform with Guidewire and Duck Creek integrations. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times by 25%, improved resolution rates at 85% STP for low-severity claims, and better reserve adequacy.

Amanda Ruiz: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new ResQ AI and InsureNext platforms, including Guidewire cloud and Salesforce Einstein, are expected to drive significant efficiencies, cost savings of $120 million YTD, and higher STP rates.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on reserve development trends?

Johnathan Hale: Thanks, Alex. As Michael detailed, we had $185 million favorable in Q2, YTD $420 million, across 85% of the portfolio. Personal auto led with $110 million, driven by severity stabilization and AI estimating. We're hardening assumptions for social inflation and expect $350-450 million FY24.

Michael Rivera: To add, accident year 2021 outperformed by 4.2 points, workers' comp via telemedicine, but prudent strengthens in E&S casualty.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jamie Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jamie Lee: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of inflation on your business?

Michael Rivera: Thanks, Jamie. Inflation headwinds like medical at 4.5% and repair/construction eased, but we've passed through 12-15% in pricing, especially auto/homeowners. Telematics and EagleEye models help manage elasticity, keeping loss ratios improving 210 bps to 62.4%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes like IFRS 17 on your underwriting strategy?

Elena Vasquez: Good question, Taylor. IFRS 17 has sharpened IBNR in Europe, contributing $35 million favorable there, especially UK motor. We've adjusted triangles and pricing, maintaining sub-93% targets while complying with Solvency II.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platforms?

Amanda Ruiz: Absolutely, Chris. ResQ AI improved reserves 15%, InsureNext $120 million savings, 85% STP claims, 40% fewer policy touchpoints via RPA. Digital quoting cuts CAC, boosts conversions 9%, positioning for scale.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: On reinsurance recoveries, any update on expected flows and program effectiveness?

Michael Rivera: Rachel, Q2 $285 million received, YTD $512 million, 96% rate. Expected $410 million outstanding, 65% highly probable. Program capped PML at 8.2%, freed $1.1 billion capital, with diversified layers and AI notifications accelerating cash.

Operator: Our next question from David Wong with Citigroup.

David Wong: Thoughts on CAC trends and new business volume?

Michael Rivera: CAC at $218, down 14% YoY via digital 62% mix, embedded at $142. New business APE $2.8 billion +18%, 1.25 million policies, led by auto $850 million telematics-driven.

Operator: One more from Sarah Ellis with Barclays.

Sarah Ellis: Share repurchases and expense ratio details?

Michael Rivera: $750 million Q3, YTD $2.8 billion accretive at $48.75. Expense 28.5%, commissions down 50 bps, operating leverage from $450 million tech roadmap.

Operator: That concludes the Q&A.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Horizon Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
